transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Ravi Patel, Lina Gomez (Redwood); Alex Torres, Priya Nair, Samir Gupta, Diane Holt (VanguardPay)

Summary:
Short discovery to scope latency/throughput requirements for real-time fraud scoring. Customer leaning towards Dedicated for predictability but wants Hosted for initial fast time-to-value; also exploring Private for regulated data in EU.

Topics discussed:
- Target p95 for scoring calls (200-300ms?)
- Concurrency: expected 300-800 concurrent scoring requests; burst to 1500/day during peaks
- Streaming vs non-streaming responses, partial outputs and early exit when confidence high
- Token/sec framing: short prompts (~30-80 tokens) but high QPS, benchmarking for tokens/sec and tokens per second per GPU
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, VPC/private control plane
- Next steps and pilot/benchmark plan

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh, quick intros? 
[00:06] Alex Torres: Hi Alex here, I'm CTO at VanguardPay, Priya's on, Samir and Diane are with me. 
[00:10] Priya Nair: Priya, Head of ML, we run the fraud model and the scoring service. 
[00:14] Maya Chen: Great. Ravi from our infra team will focus on latency and benchmarking, Lina is covering success criteria and pilot ops. 
[00:22] Ravi Patel: Hi all, glad to be here. Quick Q to start — what's your current SLOs for p95 and maybe p99 for the scoring path? 
[00:30] Priya Nair: Right now p95 is about 250ms for the on-path scoring within our microservice, but that's without large external context. For ML inference, we want to keep external call p95 below 300, ideally 200 for our highest tier. 
[00:43] Samir Gupta: We have about 500 concurrent scoring threads during peak, with short inputs ~40 tokens on average. We also have spikes to ~1k concurrency for promo windows. 
[00:56] Maya Chen: Got it. So target p95 200-300ms, concurrency typical 500, bursts to 1k. Are requests streaming or do you need streaming partial tokens? 
[01:05] Diane Holt: For fraud scoring it's mostly single-shot JSON outputs, but for troubleshooting we'd like token streaming when we do interactive investigations. Not critical for the real-time path. 
[01:18] Alex Torres: Cost is also important — we can't triple infra spend. Predictability trumps marginally lower unit-cost if it means reliability. 
[01:26] Ravi Patel: Makes sense. For those p95 numbers, we usually suggest Dedicated for predictable throughput. Hosted can work for initial evals but you get noisy co-tenancy; Private if you need on-prem or strict data residency. 
[01:39] Priya Nair: Can you share baseline numbers? Like tokens per second per GPU, typical p95 for 8k contexts vs 2k contexts, and how batching impacts latency at our average sequence lengths? 
[01:52] Ravi Patel: Sure. Quick, uh, ballpark: on a modern A100/Infer or equivalent, small prompts (<=80 tokens) with optimized runtime and continuous batching we often see p95 in the 120-220ms range at modest concurrency with quantized weights. But that heavily depends on model variant, seq length, and batching. 
[02:08] Samir Gupta: Do you have numbers for Mistral or Llama2 open weights? We may want to use open models. 
[02:15] Maya Chen: We benchmark across curated open models — Llama2, Mistral, and a few optimized weights. One note: sometimes transcripts and automated exports write KV cache as 'K V cash' — sorry, inside voice. 
[02:27] Priya Nair: (laughs) noted. 
[02:30] Ravi Patel: For benchmarking, we recommend a token/sec harness that simulates your concurrency and sequence distribution. We'll provide a script that can run on your environment or ours. For dedicated, we can provision GPU pools sized to meet 200ms p95 at 500 concurrent streams. 
[02:47] Alex Torres: What's the tradeoff between batching and latency? If you batch aggressively you reduce cost but increase p95. 
[02:54] Ravi Patel: Exactly. We have adaptive batching configured in the runtime — it tries to keep latency SLOs by controlling max batch wait. You can set a hard p95 SLO and the router will prioritize latency over throughput, or vice versa. For example, to hit p95=200ms at 500 concurrency we may set max batch size to X and batch wait to 5-10ms; we'll model this in the benchmark. 
[03:14] Priya Nair: Can you do streaming partial tokens? We want to display intermediary confidence scores in our ops UI. 
[03:20] Maya Chen: Yes, streaming is supported on Hosted and Dedicated; Private supports streaming if the on-prem runtime has the streaming hooks enabled. Note: streaming slightly increases per-request overhead but doesn't change core p95 too much for short responses. 
[03:35] Diane Holt: Security — we are EU headquartered, need data residency and KMS with customer-managed keys. Also SOC2 and SAML SSO are required. 
[03:46] Lina Gomez: We are SOC2 compliant and support SAML/SSO and integrations with customer KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can integrate with KMS for encryption at rest and we provide audit logs routed to your SIEM. For the strictest needs Private is best. 
[04:02] Samir Gupta: If we start with Hosted for pilot, and then move to Dedicated, what's the migration path? Downtime? 
[04:09] Maya Chen: We support model pinning and consistent API layer so migration is mostly config and routing — few minutes of cutover if you're careful. We can run dual routing (canary) to validate. 
[04:18] Alex Torres: Benchmarks — we need an initial baseline test: 30k QPS? No that's too high. Sorry — realistic QPS is 500-1,200 requests per second, avg tokens 40, p95 target 200ms. 
[04:31] Ravi Patel: Okay. For 1,000 RPS with 40-token payloads, we'll size dedicated clusters and estimate tokens/sec per GPU. Our bench harness will give tokens/sec and latency curves, and recommend quantization and batch configs. 
[04:44] Priya Nair: Regarding quantization: we need to keep model quality. How do you validate no-regression vs our golden prompts? 
[04:51] Maya Chen: We integrate quality monitoring — you can upload eval sets and we run regression alerts post-quantization or after model rollouts. We can include your fraud prompts as part of the eval. 
[05:03] Samir Gupta: Any gotchas with VPC private control plane? We have strict egress rules. 
[05:08] Ravi Patel: For Private we can ship an air-gapped package or VPC peering. Usually customers with egress restrictions choose Private on prem; for cloud VPC deployments we use a customer-managed control plane and peered networking. 
[05:22] Diane Holt: What about costs — both unit and committed Dedicated pricing? 
[05:25] Maya Chen: We'll send the SKU pricing. Dedicated is reserved monthly capacity — predictable. Hosted is pay-as-you-go. Optimize tooling suggests quantization and batching to reduce unit tokens. 
[05:36] Alex Torres: Any large customers in payments? 
[05:39] Maya Chen: Yes, several payments and fintech customers — we can share anonymized references and latency case studies. 
[05:45] Priya Nair: Ok squad — what does the benchmark include? Sequence length distribution, concurrency profile, streaming vs non-streaming, p95/p99, tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens? 
[05:56] Ravi Patel: Exactly. We'll include simulated traffic, your real sample traces if you share, and a config baseline for Dedicated and Hosted. We'll also provide a 'stress' test for bursts to 1.5k concurrency. 
[06:10] Alex Torres: Timeline? We want a pilot in the next 2-3 weeks. 
[06:14] Maya Chen: We can get the pilot running within two weeks once we have sample traffic and sign-off. Steps: send pricing + pilot docs, SE shares benchmark script, customer schedules kickoff. 
[06:24] Diane Holt: Who's owner on both sides? 
[06:27] Maya Chen: Maya for commercial; Ravi for benchmarking and technical. 
[06:31] Priya Nair: Samir will own infra side to provide traces. 
[06:35] (brief cross-talk) 
[06:40] Ravi Patel: Quick technical aside — for token/sec we instrument both the runtime and the router; we measure tokens per second per GPU and end-to-end p95. For streaming, we measure partial token latency and final token latency. 
[06:54] Alex Torres: Any requirements on client library or we call a REST endpoint? 
[06:58] Maya Chen: REST/SDK both supported. For low-latency we recommend gRPC or our low-overhead streaming SDK. 
[07:06] Samir Gupta: We'll likely use gRPC and keep connections warm. 
[07:10] Priya Nair: On model selection, if we pick a smaller model to hit 200ms p95 that's fine as long as fraud accuracy holds. How do you recommend A/B for accuracy-latency tradeoffs? 
[07:20] Ravi Patel: We support canary rollouts and traffic splitting. You can route X% to a faster, quantized model and monitor drift vs your golden set. If quality drops, automatic fallback to a safer variant. 
[07:33] Diane Holt: Audit logs for model ops — we need per-request logging but not PII. 
[07:39] Lina Gomez: We can mask PII and provide request/response metadata to your SIEM with opt-in redaction and audit trails in Dedicated/Private. 
[07:50] Alex Torres: Ok let's recap next steps. 
[07:52] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya sends pricing and Dedicated SKUs; Ravi shares benchmark harness and recommended configs; VanguardPay to send sample traffic and SSO/KMS contacts. Pilot kickoff target ~2026-06-18 to 20. Any outstanding questions? 
[08:06] Priya Nair: One more: do you support custom kernels and compilers for specialized hardware? We might want to test on H100 in the future. 
[08:14] Ravi Patel: Yes, we compile kernels and have GPU-specific optimizations; H100 support is available in Dedicated and Private depending on provider. We'll include recommendations. 
[08:24] Alex Torres: Thanks all. 
[08:26] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs and action items. 

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-heard words and filler; some speaker labels normalized)

End of call.
